vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: variflight-aviation
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle provides flight information services by integrating with VariFlight and AviationStack APIs. It is classified as suspicious due to high-risk execution patterns, specifically the use of 'child_process.spawn' and 'execSync' in 'src/lib/mcp-server-manager.js' and 'src/lib/aviationstack-client.js' to run 'npx' and 'uvx' commands. These commands are used to dynamically download and execute remote packages (e.g., '@variflight-ai/variflight-mcp'), which, while aligned with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) architecture, introduces significant supply chain and RCE risks. No evidence of intentional malice, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection was found. Notable IOCs include api.aviationstack.com and ai.variflight.com.

llm.summary: The skill's documentation claims it uses VariFlight MCP, but the shipped code and configuration repeatedly reference AviationStack/uvx and inconsistent environment variable names—these mismatches are unexplained and warrant caution before installing or providing API keys.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and README present the skill as a VariFlight/Variflight MCP integration (npx @variflight-ai/variflight-mcp, X_VARIFLIGHT_KEY, ai.variflight.com). Many source files (cli.js, src/lib/aviationstack-client.js, config-loader.js, README/package.json) however reference AviationStack, aviationstack-mcp, and AVIATION_STACK_API_KEY and start tools via uvx. The declared registry metadata lists no required env vars but the runtime throws if an API key isn't provided. This inconsistency between claimed provider (VariFlight) and implemented provider (AviationStack/uvx) is not proportional to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions ask the agent to read config.local.json and environment variables (normal for API keys) and to run MCP servers via npx/uvx. However the SKILL.md instructs npx @variflight-ai/variflight-mcp while aviationstack-client spawns uvx aviationstack-mcp via stdio transport—different execution paths. The SKILL.md also contains a pre-scan prompt-injection signal (unicode-control-chars) which could be used to hide or alter visible instructions. No other broad file/credential access was found in the instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no explicit install spec in the registry (instruction-only), but the package includes Node.js source and a package.json. SKILL.md recommends using npx to fetch an MCP npm package (moderate risk because npx downloads code at runtime). The code path actually uses uvx (a Python tool) and execSync('which uvx') — relying on external tools and potentially executing a Python MCP server. The mixed install/run instructions are inconsistent and increase operational uncertainty.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars, but SKILL.md declares X_VARIFLIGHT_KEY, README emphasizes X_VARIFLIGHT_KEY, and config-loader accepts AVIATION_STACK_API_KEY, X_VARIFLIGHT_KEY, or VARIFLIGHT_API_KEY. The code will throw if no API key is found and the CLI help references AVIATION_STACK_API_KEY. Multiple, conflicting env var names for different providers are requested without justification, making it unclear which credential (and to which service) you should supply.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always:true' or attempt to modify other skills or system-wide settings. Permissions in SKILL.md are limited to network, env-read, and file-read which are typical for an API-integrating skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Do not install or supply API keys until the author clarifies the real backend and env-var expectations. Specific actions to consider:
- Ask the publisher which MCP provider is used (VariFlight vs AviationStack) and which exact environment variable to set. The code and docs currently conflict.
- Inspect src/lib/variflight-client.js (not shown here) and src/lib/aviationstack-client.js to confirm which remote endpoints will receive your API key and what subprocesses will be spawned (npx vs uvx). Request the author to remove or explain the dual-provider logic.
- Verify any npm package mentioned (e.g., @variflight-ai/variflight-mcp) on the npm registry and the uvx Python package before running npx/uvx; running npx downloads and executes third-party code.
- Because SKILL.md contained unicode control characters, open the file in a hex-aware editor to ensure there is no hidden/injected content or instructions.
- If you must test, run the skill in an isolated environment or container, and do not reuse privileged or production API keys. Prefer creating a minimal/test API key with limited quota and scope.
- If the author cannot explain the mismatches, treat the package as untrusted and avoid providing real credentials.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: Scanner detected unicode control characters in SKILL.md; these can be used to obfuscate or manipulate displayed instructions. This is not expected or necessary for a straightforward flight-info skill and should be investigated.
